27777-lafayette.title: Lafayette
27777-lafayette.creator: Martha Foote Crow
27777-lafayette.description: A book by Martha Foote Crow. Among the rugged Auvergne Mountains, in the southern part of France, stands a castle that is severe and almost grim in its aspect. Two bare round towers flank the building on the right and on the left.

arxiv-2011-09526.title: Contextual Fusion For Adversarial Robustness
arxiv-2011-09526.creator: Aiswarya Akumalla, Seth Haney, Maxim Bazhenov
arxiv-2011-09526.description: Abstract Mammalian brains handle complex reasoning tasks in a gestalt manner by integrating information from regions of the brain that are specialised to individual sensory modalities. This allows for improved robustness and better generalisation ability. In contrast, deep neural networks are usually designed to process one particular information stream and susceptible to various types of adversarial perturbations.

arxiv-2103-10890.title: Simulation techniques for modified gravity
arxiv-2103-10890.creator: Claudio Llinares
arxiv-2103-10890.description: Abstract The standard paradigm of cosmology assumes General Relativity (GR) is a valid theory for gravity at scales in which it has not been properly tested. Developing novel tests of GR and its alternatives is crucial if we want to give strength to the model or find departures from GR in the data.

arxiv-2104-02959.title: The Emergence of Abstract and Episodic Neurons in Episodic Meta-RL
arxiv-2104-02959.creator: Badr AlKhamissi, Muhammad ElNokrashy, Michael Spranger
arxiv-2104-02959.description: Abstract In this work, we analyze the reinstatement mechanism introduced by Ritter et al. 2018 to reveal two classes of neurons that emerge in the agent’s working memory (an epLSTM cell) when trained using episodic meta-RL on an episodic variant of the Harlow visual fixation task.

arxiv-2203-07462.title: Jets and Jet Substructure at Future Colliders
arxiv-2203-07462.creator: Johan Bonilla, Grigorios Chachamis, Barry M. Dillon, Sergei V. Chekanov, Robin Erbacher, Loukas Gouskos, Andreas Hinzmann, Stefan Höche, B. Todd Huffman, Ashutosh. V. Kotwal, Deepak Kar, Roman Kogler, Clemens Lange, Matt LeBlanc, Roy Lemmon, Christine McLean, Benjamin Nachman, Mark S. Neubauer, Tilm
arxiv-2203-07462.description: Abstract Even though jet substructure was not an original design consideration for the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiments, it has emerged as an essential tool for the current physics program. We examine the role of jet substructure on the motivation for and design of future energy frontier colliders.

arxiv-2205-14626.title: Two-body Baryonic B u , d , s B_{u,d,s} and B c B_{c} to Charmless Final State Decays
arxiv-2205-14626.creator: Chun-Khiang Chua
arxiv-2205-14626.description: Abstract We study the rates and direct CP violations of two-body baryonic B ¯ u , d , s → 𝐁 ​ 𝐁 ¯ ′ \bar{B}_{u,d,s}\to{{\rm\bf B}\overline{\rm\bf B}}^{\prime} and B c − → 𝐁 ​ 𝐁 ¯ ′ B^{-}_{c}\to{{\rm\bf B}\overline{\rm\bf B}}^{\prime} decays, where the final state baryons include low-lying octet and decuplet baryons.

arxiv-2208-00860.title: Gaia-supported re-discovery of a remarkable weak line quasar from a variability and proper motion survey Thanks: Based on observations with the 2.2 m telescope of the German-Spanish Astronomical Center, Calar Alto, jointly operated by the Max-Planck-Institut für Astronomie Heidelberg and the Institu
arxiv-2208-00860.creator: Helmut Meusinger and Ralf-Dieter Scholz
arxiv-2208-00860.description: Abstract We demonstrate that VPMS J170850.95+433223.7 is a weak line quasar (WLQ) which is remarkable in several respects. It was already classified as a probable quasar two decades ago, but with considerable uncertainty. The non-significant proper motion and parallax from the Gaia early data release 3 have solidified this assumption. Based on previously unpublished spectra, we show that VPMS J170850.95+433223.

arxiv-2405-13694.title: Gaussian Time Machine: A Real-Time Rendering Methodology for Time-Variant Appearances
arxiv-2405-13694.creator: Licheng Shen, Ho Ngai Chow, Lingyun Wang, Tong Zhang, Mengqiu Wang, Yuxing Han
arxiv-2405-13694.description: Abstract Recent advancements in neural rendering techniques have significantly enhanced the fidelity of 3D reconstruction. Notably, the emergence of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has marked a significant milestone by adopting a discrete scene representation, facilitating efficient training and real-time rendering. Several studies have successfully extended the real-time rendering capability of 3DGS to dynamic scenes.

arxiv-2502-20764.title: Visual Attention Exploration in Vision-Based Mamba Models
arxiv-2502-20764.creator: Junpeng Wang Visa Research, Chin-Chia Michael Yeh Visa Research, Uday Singh Saini Visa Research, Mahashweta Das Visa Research
arxiv-2502-20764.description: Abstract State space models (SSMs) have emerged as an efficient alternative to transformer-based models, offering linear complexity that scales better than transformers. One of the latest advances in SSMs, Mamba, introduces a selective scan mechanism that assigns trainable weights to input tokens, effectively mimicking the attention mechanism.

arxiv-2507-00121.title: Searching for Di-Higgs Signatures of Light Charged Scalars Preprint: ZU-TH 46/25
arxiv-2507-00121.creator: Guglielmo Coloretti, Andreas Crivellin, Syuhei Iguro
arxiv-2507-00121.description: Abstract The excess in t → b ​ b ¯ ​ c t\to b\overline{b}c observed by ATLAS points towards a charged Higgs boson with a mass around 130 GeV, consistent with the expectations from the B B anomalies, i.e. R D ( ∗ ) R_{D^{(*)}} and b → s ​ ℓ + ​ ℓ − b\to s\ell^{+}\ell^{-} data.

arxiv-2510-19804.title: Forbidden Sidon subsets of perfect difference sets, featuring a human-assisted proof
arxiv-2510-19804.creator: Boris Alexeev, Dustin G. Mixon
arxiv-2510-19804.description: Abstract We resolve a $1000 Erdős prize problem, complete with formal verification generated by a large language model. In over a dozen papers, beginning in 1976 and spanning two decades, Paul Erdős repeatedly posed one of his “favourite” conjectures: every finite Sidon set can be extended to a finite perfect difference set.

pmc-11080360.title: Patient education interventions for haemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis catheter care: An integrative review
pmc-11080360.creator: Felice Fangie Leong, Fazila Binte Abu Bakar Aloweni, Jason Chon Jun Choo, Siew Hoon Lim
pmc-11080360.description: BackgroundInadequate training on how to care for haemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis catheters can lead to mechanical issues with the catheters and infectious complications (such as peritonitis) that could endanger patient safety, reduce the effectiveness of the dialysis treatment, and have a negative impact on patient morbidity and mortality.

pmc-12475671.title: Paper 17: Outcomes After Achilles Tendon Ruptures while Playing Pickleball
pmc-12475671.creator: Caroline Chen, Kiera Balding, Carissa Dock, Jacquelyn E. Fritz, Kayla J. Seiffert, Rebecca Stone McGaver, William M. Engasser, Jeffrey D. Seybold
pmc-12475671.description: Objectives:Achilles tendon ruptures are one of the most common types of tendon ruptures, and over the decades have increased in prevalence, a phenomenon credited to increasing levels of athletic activities in adults.1,2 Heavy loading and high-speed eccentric muscle action, such as sudden acceleration in running or jumping, put the Achilles tendon under stress and can lead to rupture.

pmc-12574312.title: Home visiting intervention over pregnancy and the first two years of life to promote healthy feeding practices and energy balance-related behaviors and prevent obesity risk in children from socially disadvantaged families: protocol for a participant-blinded, two-arm, parallel-group randomized contro

pmc-12574312.description: BackgroundSocial inequalities in health emerge early in life. The French Malin program, a multi-behavioral and multilevel intervention targeting both individual and structural factors, was co-created by participatory approaches involving diverse stakeholders. These stakeholders include end-users, the French Red Cross, non-profit associations, and two French pediatric societies.

pmc-12584852.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Regarding Cardiac Rehabilitation Among Patients with Chronic Heart Failure and Their Families: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-12584852.creator: Xiaohua Gao, Jianzhou Yang, Wenjun Cao, Yaoqiang Liu, Tingting Zhao
pmc-12584852.description: PurposeChronic heart failure (CHF) impairs heart function and affects patients’ well-being, while cardiac rehabilitation (CR) improves outcomes. In this cross-sectional survey, we assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) related to CR in patients with CHF and their family caregivers.Patients and MethodsA cross-sectional survey was conducted at Heping Hospital, affiliated with Changzhi Medical College, from July 1 to October 10, 2024.

pmc-13146082.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026LB128 LB128 - EFFECTS OF INTENSIVE BLOOD PRESSURE LOWERING ON COGNITIVE FUNCTION AND DEMENTIA IN PATIENTS WITH INTRACEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE: TRIDENT RESULTS
pmc-13146082.creator: Craig Anderson, Carlos Delfino, Michael O'sullivan, Michael Barnett, Floris Schreuder, Catharina Jm Klijn, Octavio Marques Pontes-Neto, Rustam Salman, Asita de Silva, Anthony Rodgers
pmc-13146082.description: Background and aimsSuvivors of intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) are at high-risk of subsequent cognitive impairment and dementia. We aimed to determine the effects of more intensive long-term blood pressure (BP) lowering with a novel single ‘triple-pill’ (fixed low-dose combination of telmisartan 20mg, amlodipine 2.5mg and indapamide1.25mg) versus placebo on cognitive function/dementia in patients with ICH.

pmc-13324242.title: Carbonyl stress markers are associated with binge‐eating/purging behavior of anorexia nervosa: A pilot study
pmc-13324242.creator: Kana Morimoto, Masanori Isobe, Tomomi Noda, Keima Tose, Momo Sunada, Koichi Tabata, Momoka Taniguchi, Makoto Arai, Toshiya Murai
pmc-13324242.description: AimAnorexia nervosa (AN) is a severe psychiatric disorder causing life‐threatening physical conditions. Management strategies differ between the restricting subtype (ANR) and the binge‐eating/purging subtype (ANBP), with underreported binge‐eating/purging behaviors. Objective biomarkers are needed to detect these behaviors for improved treatment.

pmc-13382202.title: Free will belief predicts everyday punitiveness across 44 countries
pmc-13382202.creator: Aaron Walton, Kelly Kirkland, Brock Bastian
pmc-13382202.description: Belief in free will has been linked to more punitive and retributive responses to wrongdoing. While past research has focused on North American samples and criminal contexts, this study tested whether free will belief predicts punitiveness across diverse cultural contexts and focuses on more everyday moral transgressions.

pmc-13690310.creator: Sukanth Kumar Enmozhi, Sasikala Natarajamani, Gunapriya Raghunath, Jerrine Joseph, Infant Xavier, Theepan Raaj, S. Pradeep, Niloy Raj Kalita, Sumathy Arockiasamy, Radha Vembu, Ananda Rani
pmc-13690310.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background:Density gradient sperm preparation may induce oxidative stress, impairing sperm function and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) integrity.Aim:To formulate and test an antioxidant-supplemented sperm wash with proteins.Settings and Design:An in vitro pilot proof of concept with a paired sample design.Materials and Methods:Ten normal and 10 abnormal semen samples were processed by double density gradient centrifugation of the sperm and then split into two portions that were placed in basal Ham’s F10 and in an antioxidant-enriched medium (L-carnitine, N-acetyl cysteine and D-aspartic acid).
